questions.stem: What is identified as the biggest challenge organisations face in today's technological landscape, motivating the Data and AI Cognitive (DAC) Architecture?
options: Data integration and maintainability
A shortage of dashboards
The cost of office space
Too few programming languages
The decline of relational databases
questions.explanation: The biggest challenge is data integration and maintainability, as organisations grapple with exponential data growth and widespread AI adoption.

questions.stem: What primary issue with traditional architectures does DAC Architecture aim to overcome?
options: Too much automation of AI deployment
The fragmentation of data and AI systems into separate silos, with data managed in one architecture and AI models in another
Excessive centralisation of all data in one place
The lack of any cloud services
The absence of business intelligence tools
questions.explanation: Traditional architectures treat data and AI as distinct entities in separate silos, creating significant friction; DAC unifies them.

questions.stem: What is the Data and AI Cognitive (DAC) Architecture?
options: A machine learning algorithm for image recognition
A relational database schema for finance
A next-generation unified framework that seamlessly supports both data and AI architectures, breaking down the silos between them
A project management methodology
A vendor-specific cloud product
questions.explanation: DAC Architecture is a next-generation unified framework supporting both data and AI architectures, enabling organisations to break down traditional silos.

questions.stem: Which DAC capability empowers stakeholders with secure, role-based data access while maintaining strong governance?
options: Cost Segregation and Recovery
Scalability and Flexibility
Interoperability
Data Ownership and Accessibility
Unified Data and AI Architecture
questions.explanation: Data Ownership and Accessibility empowers stakeholders with secure, role-based data access while maintaining strong governance for collaboration.

questions.stem: What do the Cost Segregation and Recovery mechanisms of DAC Architecture provide?
options: Automatic deletion of unused data
Free cloud storage
A single flat fee for all business units
Role-based access to data
Precise cost tracking, allocation and optimisation of resources
questions.explanation: Cost Segregation and Recovery allows precise cost tracking, allocation and optimisation of resources, supporting financial transparency.

questions.stem: What is the role of the Integration Hub in DAC Architecture?
options: It acts as a single source for data from multiple systems, so business units access pre-integrated data without building separate pipelines
It stores AI models only
It replaces the data governance practice
It provides read-only views for consumers
It bills business units for compute usage
questions.explanation: The Integration Hub is a single source for data from multiple systems, letting business units access pre-integrated data without separate pipelines.

questions.stem: How does the Integration Hub reduce the risk of data leakage and vulnerabilities?
options: By deleting sensitive data
By establishing a single connection to each source system
By allowing each business unit its own connection to every source
By disabling all external access
By copying data into every Business Zone
questions.explanation: By establishing a single connection to each source system, the Integration Hub minimises the risk of data leakage and vulnerabilities.

questions.stem: In DAC Architecture, what does the Virtualization Layer do?
options: It trains machine learning models
It ingests raw data from source systems
It manages all read-only views across Enterprise and Business Zones, serving as a unified platform for data consumers
It stores the governance blueprint
It allocates cloud costs to departments
questions.explanation: The Virtualization Layer manages all read-only views across Enterprise and Business Zones and serves as the unified platform for data consumers.

questions.stem: In DAC Architecture, which body manages the blueprint for all standards, policies, metadata, data quality, privacy and security controls, and data lifecycle management?
options: The Integration Hub
The Virtualization Layer
Each Business Zone independently
The Centralised Data Governance Practice (Data Practice Management Team)
The external cloud provider
questions.explanation: The Centralised Data Governance Practice manages the blueprint for standards, policies, metadata, data quality, privacy and security controls, and lifecycle management for the Enterprise and Business Zones.

questions.stem: How do the Business Zone (BZ) Data Governance Practices relate to the Centralised Data Governance Practice in DAC Architecture?
options: The BZ practices have no governance responsibilities at all
The BZ practices override the central practice
The central practice manages every BZ decision directly
The BZ practices report only to the Integration Hub
Each BZ practice has its own data stewardship and manages its specific standards, adhering to best practices shared by the central practice, which regularly reviews them
questions.explanation: Enterprise and Business Zones each have dedicated data stewardships; BZ practices manage their own standards while following central best practices, and the central practice regularly evaluates them.
